p0.original: 第十二章 重获生活的热情

p2.original: 在成长的过程中，我们学习了许多无益的知识，这些知识来自善意的父母、老师或别的人。由于这些教诲看起来是那样地天经地义，我们也就不再去探讨它们的合理性。喜剧演员巴迪·哈克特（Buddy Hackett）曾在一档娱乐节目中说，小时候每天吃着妈妈做的丰盛的饭菜，直到去军中服役，他才知道饭后胃部还可以保持轻松。同样的，我们在社会文化影响下形成的一些不良积习，渗透到了生活的各个方面，以致我们觉察不到它们的存在。只有深入了解我们的生存状态，我们才能看清它们的危害，并形成新的想法及行为方式，来满足身心健康的需要。
p2.en: As we grow up, we learn a lot of unhelpful knowledge from goodwill parents, teachers or others. As these teachings seem to be so divine, we will not discuss their legitimacy. The comedian Buddy Hackett had said in a entertainment show that when he was a child, he ate her mother's good meals every day, until he was in the army, and he knew that his stomach was still easy after dinner. Similarly, some of the negative habits that we have developed under socio-cultural influences permeate all aspects of life, so that we do not see their existence. It is only with an in-depth understanding of our very existence that we will be able to see their dangers and to develop new ideas and ways of behaviour to meet the needs of physical and mental health.

p3.original: 然而，对于大多数人来说，倾听和表达自己的需要并不容易。一般来说，我们的文化倾向于把个人需要看作是消极的、具有破坏性的。如果一个人公开表达自己的需要，就很可能被看作是自私的。
p3.en: However, it is not easy for most people to listen to and express their needs. Generally speaking, our culture tends to view individual needs as negative and destructive. If a person publicly expresses his or her needs, he or she is likely to be seen as selfish.

p4.original: 通过鼓励我们区分观察和评论，认识情感的根源在于个人的需要和想法，并以建设性的语言提出明确的请求，非暴力沟通帮助我们认识社会文化对个体的消极影响。一旦认识到社会文化的局限性，我们就可能突破它的束缚，至少，我们已经迈出了关键的一步。
p4.en: By encouraging us to distinguish between observations and comments, recognizing that the roots of emotion lie in the needs and thoughts of individuals, and making clear requests in constructive language, Nonviolent Communication helps us to understand the negative impact of socio-cultural processes on individuals. Once we have realized the limitations of our culture, we may have broken through its constraints, at least we have taken a crucial step.

p6.original: 在生活中，有时我们会感到沮丧，觉得前途一片黑暗。欧内斯特·贝克（Ernest Becker）在他的《精神病学的革命》一书中提出，沮丧是因为一个人处于激烈的内心冲突之中，无所适从。我们内心中也许有一种声音说，“我想这样做”；但又有一种声音说，“不，你不应该那样做”。这样，我们就陷入了僵局。沮丧意味着，我们不了解自己的需要——我们不知道自己到底想要什么以及如何满足愿望。
p6.en: In life, we sometimes feel frustrated and have a dark future. Ernest Becker, in his book " The Revolution of Psychiatry ", argued that frustration was due to the fact that a person was in a deep internal conflict and was in a state of discomfort. There may be a voice in our hearts that says, "I want to do this." But another voice said, “No, you shouldn't have done that”. In this way, we are in a stalemate. Frustration means that we do not know our needs — we do not know exactly what we want and how to meet them.

p7.original: 一位学习非暴力沟通的女士有一段时间心情很不好。一位朋友建议她在心情极度沮丧时以对话的形式记录内心的挣扎。以下是前两句：
p7.en: A woman who learned Nonviolent Communication had been in a bad mood for some time. A friend suggested that she record her struggle in dialogue when she is in deep depression. The first two sentences are as follows:

p8.original: 声音1（“职业女性”）：“我应该在工作上投入更多的时间。我受了这么好的教育，我也相信自己的才干，但现在都白白浪费了。”
p8.en: Voice 1 (“Professional Woman”): “I should invest more time in my work. I have been so well educated and I believe in my talents, but now I am wasted.

p9.original: 声音2（“负责任的母亲”）：“你太不现实了。你是两个孩子的母亲，你都没法照顾好他们，还好意思谈别的？”
p9.en: Voice 2 ( "Responsible Mother"): "You're too unrealistic. You're the mother of two children. You can't take care of them. You want to talk about something else?

p10.original: 几个月来，这位女士就一直生活在激烈的思想斗争之中，她的头脑中充斥着各种对自己的批评和指责。看到这段对话后，她的朋友又建议她，让心中的那位“职业女性”用非暴力沟通表达自己。
p10.en: For months, the woman had been living in a fierce intellectual struggle, filled with criticisms and accusations against herself. After seeing this conversation, her friends suggested that she should allow the “working woman” in her heart to express herself through Nonviolent Communication.

p11.original: 于是，她就用非暴力沟通的四个要素来表达“职业女性”的心声：“为了照顾孩子，我放弃了工作，留在家里（观察）；我有点心灰意冷（感受），因为我看重成就感（需要）。我想，我现在也许可以去找份兼职（请求）。”
p11.en: So she used the four elements of Nonviolent Communication to express the “working woman”'s voice: “I gave up work and stayed at home (observation) in order to take care of the child; I'm a little depressed (feeling) because I value the sense of achievement (need). I think I might be able to get a part-time job right now.

p12.original: 接着，她用非暴力沟通的四个要素来表达“负责任的母亲”的心声：“当我想到上班的事情时（观察），我好害怕（感受），因为我要确保孩子们能得到很好的照顾（需要）。我想，在上班时，我需要一位好保姆来照顾他们。下班后，我还要确保有时间和精力好好陪孩子。”
p12.en: She then used four elements of Nonviolent Communication to express the voice of “responsible mothers”: “When I think about what I do at work (observation), I'm scared (fear), because I want to ensure that children are well cared for (needs). I think I need a good nanny to take care of them at work. After work, I also have to make sure I have time and energy to stay with the kids.

p13.original: 当这位女士用非暴力沟通的方式说出心里话后，她大大松了一口气。她没有再批评和指责自己，而把注意力放在了自己的感受和需要上。虽然她还有实际的问题需要处理，例如找个好保姆、寻求先生的支持，但她已经察觉到自己的需要，并能静下心来采取必要的行动。
p13.en: When the woman spoke in her heart in a non-violent way, she was relieved. Instead of criticizing and accusing herself, she focused on her feelings and needs. While she still had practical problems to address, such as finding a good nanny and seeking his support, she had already felt her needs and was able to take the necessary action in a quiet manner.

p15.original: 如果以苛刻的态度对人对己，我们的心情也好不到哪里去。通过运用非暴力沟通，我们不再试图分析自己或他人有什么毛病，而是用心去了解我们的需要，这样，我们的内心就会逐渐变得平和。
p15.en: We are not in a better mood if we treat ourselves harshly. By using Nonviolent Communication, we no longer attempt to analyse what is wrong with ourselves or others, but rather to understand our needs with our hearts, so that our hearts will gradually become calm.

p16.original: 为了能够更好地照顾自己，一位女士报名参加了一个历时三天的非暴力沟通研讨班。在活动期间，她发现自己的生活态度有了明显的改变。她回忆说，在第二天清晨醒来时，她头痛得十分厉害。“在过去，我的第一反应就是去检讨自己到底做错了什么。是否吃了不好的食物？是不是给自己施加了太大的压力？我会盘问自己诸如此类的问题。这一次，在学习了非暴力沟通之后，我问自己的问题是，‘我现在需要做什么来缓解头痛’。”
p16.en: In order to be able to take better care of herself, a woman enrolled in a three-day workshop on Nonviolent Communication. During the campaign, she found a marked change in her life attitude. She recalled that she had a very severe headache when she woke up the following morning. “In the past, my first reaction was to examine what I had done wrong. Did you eat bad food? Did you put too much pressure on yourself? I'll question myself about things like that. This time, after learning about Nonviolent Communication, I asked myself, "What do I need to do now to ease my headache?"

p17.original: “我坐了起来，做了一些柔和的头部运动。接着，起床到外面走了走，回来后又做了一些别的事情，让自己放松下来。过了一会儿，头没那么痛了。这时，我想了想昨天在研讨班中的经历。我发现，头痛很可能是因为昨天我不怎么留意身体的状态。现在，身体是通过头痛来提醒我‘请留意我的需要’。于是，在接下来两天的研讨班中，我就用心体会身体的状态，并注意调节和放松。这一次的经历提醒我：在头痛时，我可以专注于我的需要。这是我人生的重大突破。”
p17.en: "I sat up and made some soft head movement. Then he got up and walked outside and came back and did something else to relax himself. After a while, it didn't hurt that much. At that point, I thought about what I had in the seminar yesterday. I found out that the headaches were probably due to yesterday's insensitive state of mind. Now, the body reminds me of my needs through headaches. So, for the next two days, I'm going to have to see my body, and I'm going to be careful to regulate and relax. This experience reminds me of the fact that I can focus on my needs when my head hurts. This is a major breakthrough in my life.

p18.original: 在另一次研讨班中，有个参加者询问如何在开车时保持良好的心态。这是我很熟悉的问题！由于工作的需要，我过去经常开车前往美国各地。我知道，在开车时，保持良好的心态有多困难。那时，如果有人以我不喜欢的方式开车，我的头脑中常常会冒出以下的想法：“这家伙有毛病！开车都不看路？”带着这样的想法，我就会想好好教训那些我认为不守规矩的司机。可是，我又没法惩罚他们，于是，就更加恼怒了。
p18.en: In another workshop, one participant asked how to maintain a good mind when driving. That's a familiar question! I used to drive all over the United States because of the need for work. I know how hard it is to keep a good mind when driving. At that time, if someone drives in a way I don't like, my mind often comes up with the following idea: "This guy's got a problem! You're not even looking at the road? "With this idea in mind, I'd like to teach a good lesson to the drivers who I think are not. But I couldn't punish them, so I got even more angry.

p19.original: 后来，我终于学会了关注自己的感受和需要。“是的，看到他们这样开车，我真的很害怕；我希望，他们在开车时能注意安全。”哇！我感到惊讶的是，只要我不再批评和指责他人，而把注意力放在自己的感受和需要，我的心情就放松了许多。
p19.en: Then I finally learned to look at my feelings and needs. "Yes, I'm really scared to see them drive like this. I hope they'll be safe when they drive. "Whoa! I am surprised that my mood is much relaxed as long as I stop criticizing and accusing others and focus on my feelings and needs.

p20.original: 我深受鼓舞，于是又决定去体会其他司机的感受和需要。在第一次尝试这么做的时候，我就得到了很大的满足。那一次，在我前面的那辆车开得非常慢，它在每个十字路口都会减速。我有点急了，我和自己说：“这车没法开了。”注意到自己的紧张情绪后，我开始体会那辆车的司机可能会有怎样的感受和需要。我觉得，前面的那位司机有点不知所措，希望得到后面司机的谅解。路渐渐宽了，在超车时，我发现那辆车的司机是一位看起来有80岁的老太太。她看上去惊慌失措。我很庆幸，我曾用心去体会她的感受和需要，而没有鸣喇叭或做别的动作来表达我的不悦。
p20.en: I was very encouraged and decided to feel the feelings and needs of the other drivers. When I tried to do that for the first time, I was very satisfied. That time, the car in front of me was very slow, and it slowed down at every intersection. I was in a hurry, and I said to myself, "This car can't go. I started to see how the driver of that car might feel and need it, after I noticed his stress. I think the driver in front is a little confused and would like to get an understanding from the driver in the back. The road was getting wider, and when I went over, I found that the driver of the car was an 80-year-old lady. She seemed scared. I was glad I felt her feelings and needs with my heart, and I did not sing or do anything to express my displeasure.

p21.original: 用非暴力沟通代替诊断
p21.en: Nonviolent Communication in lieu of diagnosis

p22.original: 许多年前，为了成为一名合格的心理医生，我接受了九年的培训，并获得了临床心理学博士学位。毕业后不久，我有幸旁听了以色列哲学家马丁·布伯与美国心理学家卡尔·罗杰斯关于精神疗法的讨论。在讨论中，布伯质疑，如果一个人把自己当作心理医生，他是否还能够有效地帮助他人面对心灵的创伤。布伯当时正在访问美国，他和罗杰斯一起受邀来到一所精神病院进行公开的讨论。旁听的人都是精神病学领域的专业人员。
p22.en: Many years ago, in order to become a qualified psychologist, I received nine years of training and obtained a doctorate in clinical psychology. Shortly after graduation, I had the privilege of following the discussion on psychotherapy by Israeli philosopher Martin Buber and American psychologist Carl Rogers. During the discussion, Bubble questioned whether a person who treated himself as a psychologist could still effectively help others to face the trauma of their hearts. Bubble was visiting the United States and was invited with Rogers to a psychiatric hospital for public discussion. All those listening were professionals in the field of psychiatry.

p23.original: 布伯的观点是，个人的成长是通过与他人的坦诚交流来实现的——在交流中，彼此能够自由地表达内心的软弱。他不相信，这能够存在于心理医生与其顾客之间。罗杰斯同意，坦诚是个人成长的先决条件。但是，他相信，出色的心理医生能够超越他的身份，来坦诚地与顾客交流。
p23.en: Bubble's view is that the growth of the individual is achieved through frank interaction with others — in which one can freely express one another's inner weakness. He did not believe that this could exist between the psychologist and his client. Rogers agrees that honesty is a prerequisite for personal growth. However, he is confident that a good psychologist will be able to speak frankly to his customers beyond his status.

p24.original: 布伯对此表示怀疑。他认为，只要顾客把自己看作是顾客、把医生看作是医生，即使医生愿意与顾客真诚地交流，这样的交流实际上还是不可能的。他评论说，顾客预约看病的过程，以及花钱来解决问题，使医生和顾客之间的交流很难不受其身份束缚。
p24.en: Bubble is skeptical. In his view, as long as the customer sees himself as a customer and as a doctor, even if the doctor is willing to communicate with the customer in good faith, such communication is practically impossible. He commented that the customer's appointment process and the cost of solving the problem made it difficult for doctors and customers to communicate independently of their identities.

p25.original: 他们的对话回答了我长期以来对分离疗法（Clinical Detachment）的困惑。在我所接受的教育中，分离疗法被认为是心理分析疗法的金科玉律。根据分离疗法的理论，在心理治疗的过程中，医生表达自己的感受和需要是十分不专业的；有经验的医生则会采取“冷眼旁观”的态度，在治疗过程中不带有任何感情色彩，并避免因个人内心的冲突造成对顾客的伤害——他们就像一面镜子，让顾客充分投射他们的情感，然后，他们会作出诊断。我理解分离疗法的理论。然而，对于保持与来访者情感的距离，我总是觉得不太舒服；此外，我相信，在治疗的过程中，表达个人的感受和需要是有益的。
p25.en: Their dialogue answered my long-standing confusion about the separation therapy. In the education I have received, separation therapy is considered the golden rule of psychoanalytic therapy. According to the theory of separatism, it is very unprofessional for doctors to express their feelings and needs during the psychotherapy process; Experienced doctors, for their part, take a “cold-eyed look” approach, do not have any emotional aspects of the treatment and avoid harm to their customers as a result of personal conflicts — they act as a mirror, allowing customers to project their emotions fully, and then they make a diagnosis. I understand the theory of separation therapy. However, I was not always comfortable with maintaining the distance from visitors; Furthermore, I believe that it is useful to express individual feelings and needs in the course of treatment.

p26.original: 于是，我开始试着用非暴力沟通的语言来代替医疗术语。我不再根据我所学习的心理学理论来分析来访者的心理特点，而是用心去体会他们的话，并表达自己内心的感受。在开始时，我很担心。我不知道，对我的做法，同行们会有怎样的看法。然而，效果却是非常好，不论是来访者还是我自己，都十分满意。很快，我就不再有任何顾虑了。在35年后的今天，心理医生在治疗过程中投入自己的情感，已不再被看作另类了。可是，在那时，我却经常被心理医生的团体邀请去发表演讲和做现场示范。
p26.en: So I started to try to replace medical terms with Nonviolent Communication. Instead of analysing the psychological characteristics of visitors in the light of the psychological theories that I have learned, I am trying to understand their words and express what they feel inside. At the beginning, I was worried. I don't know what my peers would think about my approach. However, the results have been very good, and both the visitors and myself have been very satisfied. Soon, I will have no more concerns. Thirty-five years later, the psychotherapy is no longer seen as an alternative to the emotionalization of the treatment. However, at that time, I was often invited by a group of psychologists to give speeches and make live demonstrations.

p27.original: 有一次，我被邀请去演示如何运用非暴力沟通来帮助处于极度痛苦中的人。地点是在一所精神病院，参加的人很多，都是精神病学领域的专业人员。讲解了一个小时后，他们请我当场会见一个病人，分析她的病情，并提供治疗建议。那是一位29岁的女士，她有3个孩子，我们谈了约半小时。在她离开房间之后，负责治疗的几位医生提出了一个问题：“卢森堡博士，请作一下判断。根据你的意见，这位女士是患精神分裂症还是药物性精神障碍？”
p27.en: On one occasion, I was invited to demonstrate how to use Nonviolent Communication to help people in extreme pain. It is located in a psychiatric hospital with a large number of participants, all specialists in the field of psychiatry. An hour later, they asked me to meet with a patient on the spot to analyse her condition and provide advice on treatment. That's a 29-year-old lady with three kids, and we talked about it for about half an hour. After she left the room, several doctors in charge of the treatment asked a question: “Dr. Luxembourg, please make a judgement. In your opinion, is the lady schizophrenic or a drug-related mental disorder?

p28.original: 我回答说，对于这类问题，我感到不太舒服。我曾在精神病院工作，但从一开始，我就无法将病人归到某种特定的精神病类别中。一些研究报告显示，精神病医生和心理学专家对那些医学术语也没有一致的意见。这些研究报告还指出，精神病医生所就读的学校比病人个人的特点对诊断的结果更具影响力。
p28.en: I replied that I was not comfortable with such questions. I worked in a psychiatric institution, but from the outset I was unable to place patients in a particular category of mental illness. Some studies indicate that there is also no agreement between psychiatrists and psychologists on those medical terms. The studies also noted that the schools attended by psychiatrists were more influential in the diagnosis than the patient's personal characteristics.

p29.original: 我进一步说，即使精神病医生对这些术语的运用具有共识，我也不想用它们，因为我看不出这么做对病人有什么好处。在物理医学领域，病理分析常常可以为治疗指明方向；但我不认为，这种方法适用于所谓的精神病学领域。根据我的经历，在医院的病例讨论会上，医生们要花大部分的时间来讨论病人是属于哪种精神病类型。当预定的讨论时间快要结束时，主治医生也许会请求其他人帮助制订医疗计划。然而，这类请求通常会被忽视，因为大多数的人倾向于继续争论。
p29.en: I went further, saying that even if there was a consensus among psychiatrists on the use of these terms, I would not want to use them, because I do not see what it would do for the patient. In the field of physics, pathology analysis can often provide direction for treatment; But I do not think that this approach applies to the so-called psychiatric field. In my experience, doctors spend most of their time discussing the type of mental illness a patient is of. When the scheduled discussion period is almost over, the attending physician may request the assistance of others in developing a medical plan. However, such requests are often ignored, as the majority tends to continue the debate.

p30.original: 接着，我向他们解释我的做法。我告诉他们，我不会去分析病人有什么毛病，而是问自己以下的问题：“她现在是什么心情？她有什么需要？和她在一起，我是什么样的心情？我的心情反映了我怎样的需要？我想请她作出什么决定或采取什么行动，以使她能快乐些？”在回答这样的问题时，我们将会揭示自己的内心活动以及个人需要。同作诊断相比，这是很不容易的，因为在这个过程中，我们也会深深体会到我们作为人的弱点。
p30.en: Then I explained to them what I did. I told them that I would not analyze what was wrong with the patient, but ask myself the following question: "What is she feeling now? What does she need? How am I feeling with her? How do I feel about my needs? What decisions or actions do I want to ask her to make her happy? “In answering such questions, we will reveal our inner activities and personal needs. This is not easy to diagnose, because in the process we will also have a deep sense of our vulnerability as human beings.

p31.original: 另有一次，我被邀请去讲解如何向精神病人介绍非暴力沟通。参加现场演示的是15位被诊断为慢性精神分裂症患者的病人。大概有80位旁观者，其中有心理学家、精神病医生、社会工作者以及修女。在我介绍自己和讲解非暴力沟通的时候，一位病人说了一句似乎与主题无关的话。考虑到他被诊断为慢性精神分裂症，我的第一反应是认为他在胡言乱语。于是，我对他说，“你好像没有听懂我刚才的意思。”
p31.en: On another occasion, I was invited to talk about Nonviolent Communication with the mentally ill. The presentation was attended by 15 patients diagnosed with chronic schizophrenia. There are approximately 80 bystanders, including psychologists, psychiatrists, social workers and nuns. When I introduced myself and spoke about Nonviolent Communication, one patient said something that seemed irrelevant to the subject. My first reaction, considering that he was diagnosed with chronic schizophrenia, was to think he was talking nonsense. So I said to him, "You don't seem to understand what I just said.

p32.original: 这时候，另一个病人插话说：“我知道他是什么意思。”接着，他向我解释那位病人的话和我刚才对非暴力沟通的介绍有什么关系。听了他的解释，我意识到那位病人的话确实和主题有关。想到自己刚才轻易地将交流中的困难归咎于对方，我感到很难过。我希望，在听不明白的时候，我可以请对方作出解释，例如：“我不太明白你的意思。我想知道你的问题和我对非暴力沟通的介绍有什么联系。你可以解释一下吗？”
p32.en: And then another patient said, "I know what he means. He then explained to me what the patient's words had to do with what I had just said about Nonviolent Communication. Listening to his explanation, I realized that the patient's words were indeed relevant to the subject. It is sad to think that I have just so easily attributed the difficulties of communication to the other side. I hope that when I don't understand, I can ask for explanations, for example: “I don't understand what you mean. I want to know how your problems relate to my introduction to Nonviolent Communication. Can you explain?

p33.original: 除了这个短暂的插曲外，整个过程进行得十分顺利。旁观者对病人的反应感到很意外。他们问我，我是否认为这组病人碰巧是特别合作的病人。我回答说，一旦我不把人当作诊断的对象，而专注于彼此作为人的感受和需要，人们通常都会有积极的反应。
p33.en: Apart from this brief episode, the process proceeded very smoothly. The bystanders were surprised by the patient's reaction. They asked me if I thought this group of patients happened to be particularly cooperative patients. I replied that, once I did not treat people as diagnostics and focused on each other's feelings and needs as human beings, people usually responded positively.

p34.original: 接着，有位参加者说，为了有更多的学习机会，他想请几位心理学家和精神病医生来参加现场演示。于是，之前参加演示的病人和旁听者中的志愿者交换了位置。在接下来的讲解中，我发现我很难向一位精神病医生解释清楚分析与倾听的区别。只要小组中有人表达自己的感受，他就开始运用精神病学的理论进行分析，而没有用心体会。当他第三次这么做的时候，在旁听席的一位病人大声喊道：“难道你看不出来你又在做同样的事情？你是在分析她讲的话，而没有用心体会她的感受！”
p34.en: Subsequently, one participant said that, in order to have more learning opportunities, he would like to invite several psychologists and psychiatrists to participate in the live demonstration. As a result, volunteers from patients who had previously participated in the demonstration exchanged places with observers. In the ensuing remarks, I found it difficult to explain to a psychiatrist the difference between analysis and listening. As long as one of the members of the group expressed his feelings, he began to use the psychiatric theory for analysis without knowing it. When he did it the third time, a patient in the gallery shouted, "Do you not see you're doing the same thing again? You're analyzing what she's saying, and you're not trying to understand how she feels!

p35.original: 通过培养非暴力沟通的意识和技巧，我们就可以在真诚、开放的气氛中与他人进行平等的互动，从而帮助他人摆脱心理的困扰。
p35.en: By developing awareness and skills for Nonviolent Communication, we can interact equally with others in an atmosphere of sincerity and openness, thus helping others to escape from psychological distress.

p37.original: 在情绪低落的时候，我们也许会怨天尤人。然而，如果我们以苛刻的态度对人对己，我们的心情也好不到哪里去。通过运用非暴力沟通，我们不再试图分析自己或他人有什么毛病，而是用心去了解我们的需要，这样，我们的内心将逐渐变得平和。一旦我们发现自己心底深处的愿望，并采取积极的行动，我们将会重获生活的热情。心理咨询和心理治疗行业的从业人员可以考虑借助非暴力沟通来与来访者进行坦诚的交流。
p37.en: We may blame God when we're depressed. However, if we treat ourselves harshly, we are not in a better mood. By using Nonviolent Communication, we no longer attempt to analyse what is wrong with ourselves or others, but rather to understand our needs with our hearts, so that our hearts will gradually be at peace. Once we discover our deep-seated aspirations and take positive action, we will regain the passion of our lives. Those involved in psychological counselling and therapy may consider using Nonviolent Communication to communicate frankly with visitors.

p40.original: 一位学习非暴力沟通的女士讲述了以下的故事。
p40.en: A woman who studied Nonviolent Communication told the following story.

p41.original: 那一天，我参加完历时十天的非暴力沟通培训回到家时，发现艾里斯正在等我。艾里斯是一所学校的图书馆管理员，她做这份工作已有25年的时间。我们是在6年前的一次极富挑战性的训练营中认识的。一见面，我就迫不及待地告诉她，我参加非暴力沟通培训的情况。这时，艾里斯告诉我，虽然已经过了6年，但只要一想起那次活动的领队在科罗拉多州对她说的话，她还会愤愤不平。我知道她说的是里芙。里芙热爱自然，能够识别动物的粪便。我还清楚地记着她攀岩时在半空中摇晃的情景，她的手掌有许多伤痕——那是被绳索割破留下的。她在黑夜中吼叫，在高兴时手舞足蹈，坦率地表达她的感受和想法。艾里斯这里提到的事情是，有一天，里芙对她说：“艾里斯，我真受不了你这样的人，不论何时，你都甜得腻死人。真是个毕恭毕敬的图书馆管理员！为什么不放下面具，直率一些呢？”
p41.en: That day, when I returned home from a 10-day Nonviolent Communication training, I found Iris waiting for me. Iris is the librarian of a school, and she has been doing this for 25 years. We met six years ago in a very challenging training camp. Upon meeting, I was anxious to tell her about my participation in Nonviolent Communication training. At that point, Iris told me that, although it had been six years, she would be outraged to remember what the leader of that event had said to her in Colorado. I know she said Liv. Liv loves nature. He can identify animal excrement. I also remember clearly the scene of her shaking in the middle of the air while climbing the rocks, and her palms were scarred — it was cut by a rope. She shouts in the dark, dances in her hands and frankly expresses her feelings and thoughts. The thing that Iris mentioned here was that one day, Riv said to her, "Iris, I can't stand people like you, you're so sweet at all times. What a humble librarian! Why don't you put down your mask and be more forthright?

p42.original: 6年来，艾里斯不断地想起里芙的这句话并在心里驳斥她。我们两个人现在都很想看看非暴力沟通对这样的情形能发挥怎样的作用。于是，由我来扮演里芙的角色。在开始时，我对艾里斯说了里芙的那句话。
p42.en: For six years, Iris kept thinking about Liv and rebukeing her. Both of us are now keen to see what Nonviolent Communication can do in such situations. So, I'll play Liv. At the beginning, I said that to Iris.

p44.original: 艾里斯：（暂不考虑非暴力沟通，她认为里芙在批评和羞辱她。）“你怎么可以这样和我说话？你并不了解我，你也不知道我是怎样的图书馆管理员！我告诉你，我很认真对待我的工作，我把自己看作是一个教育者，和其他教师并没有什么不同……”
p44.en: Iris: “Not considering Nonviolent Communication, she believes that Liv is criticizing and humiliating her. "How can you talk to me like that? You don't know me, you don't know what kind of librarian I am! I'm telling you, I take my work seriously, and I see myself as an educator, and not as much as any other teacher...”

p45.original: 我：（站在里芙的角度）“听起来，你很生气。你认为在评价别人之前要先有所了解，是吗？”
p45.en: And I'm: "Standing in the way of Liv," and you sound angry. You think you need to know something before you judge others, don't you?

p46.original: 艾里斯：“当然了！你至少应该知道我在这次训练营中的表现。你看，我现在站在这里，在过去的14天中，我没有被任何困难压倒，我成功了，不是吗？”
p46.en: Iris: Of course! You should at least know what I did in this camp. Look, I'm standing right here, and I've been out of any difficulty for the last 14 days, and I've made it, haven't I?

p47.original: 我：（继续扮演里芙）“你似乎有些伤心，你希望你所表现的勇气和耐力能够得到肯定，是这样吗？”
p47.en: I (continue to play Liv) “You seem a little sad, and you hope that your courage and endurance will be recognized, is that so?

p49.original: 我们又说了几句。这时，我发现艾里斯的状态有了一些变化。如果一个人觉得自己得到了别人的理解，他的身体就会有一些反应。例如，他可能会放松下来。一般来说，这意味着他已经充分表达他的某种痛苦，可以将注意力转向其他的话题。这样，他就可以进一步表达其他方面的感受和需要。有时，他甚至可以开始关注对方的感受和需要。不过，我注意到，艾里斯现在还处于痛苦中。毕竟，由于认为自己受了羞辱，在过去的6年中，她在心里积累了许多怨气。
p49.en: We said a few more. And then I found that Iris's state had changed a bit. If a person feels that he/she has been understood, his/her body will have some reaction. For example, he might relax. Generally speaking, this means that he has already adequately expressed some of his suffering and can turn his attention to other topics. In this way, he can further express the feelings and needs of others. Sometimes he can even begin to look at the feelings and needs of the other. I note, however, that Iris is still in pain. After all, over the past six years, she has accumulated a lot of resentment in her heart because she thinks she has been humiliated.

p51.original: 艾里斯：（在经历了微妙的心理变化后，她立即接着说）“该死！6年前，我就该和她说这番话！”
p51.en: Iris: "Damn it! I should have said that to her six years ago!

p52.original: 我：（作为一个朋友）“看来，你很后悔当时没有说出心里话？”
p52.en: And I'm: "As a friend, you seem to regret not saying what you were thinking at the time?

p53.original: 艾里斯：“我就像一个大混蛋！我知道我不是一个‘毕恭毕敬的图书馆管理员’，但我为什么没有反驳她呢？”
p53.en: Iris: "I'm like a big asshole! I know I'm not a "pompous librarian," but why didn't I refute her?

p54.original: 我：“哦，你希望能有足够的勇气表达自己？”
p54.en: I said, "Oh, you want enough courage to express yourself?

p55.original: 艾里斯：“是的。我真受不了自己！我竟然任她摆布！”
p55.en: Iris: Yes. I can't stand myself! I let her do it!

p56.original: 我：“你特别渴望能够主动表达自己？”
p56.en: I said, "Are you particularly eager to be able to express yourself?

p57.original: 艾里斯：“正是。我需要记住这一点！”
p57.en: Iris: Exactly. I need to remember that!

p59.original: 艾里斯安静了片刻。接着，她说，她现在可以开始练习非暴力沟通，试着换个角度来理解里芙的话。
p59.en: Iris was quiet for a moment. She then said that she could now begin to practice Nonviolent Communication and try to understand Liv's words from a different angle.

p61.original: 我：（扮演里芙）“艾里斯，我真受不了你这样的人，不论何时，你都甜得腻死人。真是个必恭必敬的图书馆管理员！为什么不放下面具，直率一些呢？”
p61.en: I'm like, "Iris, I can't stand people like you, you're so sweet whenever you want. What a humble librarian! Why don't you put down your mask and be more forthright?

p62.original: 艾里斯：（倾听里芙的感受、需要和请求）“哦，里芙，听起来，你有点不耐烦，你不耐烦是因为……因为我……”（这里，艾里斯用到了“因为我”，这意味着她没有去考虑里芙的哪些需要导致了里芙感到不耐烦。也就是说，在非暴力沟通中，你感到不耐烦不是因为我做了什么，而是因为你期待我有不同的行为方式。）
p62.en: Iris: "Oh, Riv, you sound a little impatient because I'm the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one who's the one. That is, in Nonviolent Communication, you are impatient not because of what I did, but because you expect me to behave differently. I don't think so.

p64.original: 这时，我努力把自己放在里芙的角度，来体会里芙到底有怎样的需要。突然，我（作为里芙）意识到了我想加深与他人的联系。“联系！我想要的是联系！……我想与你加深联系，艾里斯！你总是那样地彬彬有礼，我希望你放开一些，表达你的内心感受！”
p64.en: At that point, I tried to put myself in Liv's perspective to see what she really needed. Suddenly, I realized that I wanted to deepen my ties with others. "Contact! What I want is contact! I want to get closer to you, Iris! You're always so polite, I want you to let go and express your feelings!

p65.original: 在我喊出这段话后，我们两个人都愣住了。艾里斯说：“如果我知道她想要的是什么，如果她告诉我她想加深与我的联系……唉！那简直就是在表达爱。”虽然她无法找真正的里芙来核实我们的猜测是否正确，通过这段对话，艾里斯终于打开了心结。在那以后，在听到不中听的话时，她也开始留意那些话的真正含义。
p65.en: After I shouted that, both of us stopped. Iris said, "If I knew what she wanted, if she told me that she wanted to get closer to me...alas! That's just love. “Although she could not find a true Liv to verify that our guess was correct, through this dialogue, Iris finally opened his heart. After that, she began to look at the true meaning of those words when she heard them.
